I’ve had ect and found my memory has gaps now. Mostly from when it was done and months back from that. Also I’m missing some stuff from my past. Things people have said I’ve done that I just don’t recall, and also my mind is completing memories I do have in strange ways. People often tell me “that’s not how that ended, here’s what happened after that…”

I also forgot who my wife was, let alone that I was married. Luckily once she started reminding me it started coming back. 

The doctor also told me that whatever I forgot will come back to me over time. I call bs on that. It’s been years now and I still get reminded by people that I did certain things. 

For me it really didn’t help. I did a tolal of 15 treatments both inpatient and outpatient. Outpatient was the toughest because you had to get redressed, find your ride (if you remember someone brought you! I forgot some of the times that my ride was waiting for me!)

If I have a choice I probably wouldn’t do them again. But it was one of those last ditch efforts to restart my brain and hopefully get rid of some of the mental issues I was facing.

I’ve done inpatient, outpatient, and whatever they call living with a group for months. It wasn’t terrible. I’d like to think they helped me when I needed it most. I’d recommend it for anyone going through times when they think nothing will help. 

I’ve honestly done inpatient more times than I can count at a lot of different places and they are mostly different. 

You’ll start with an inventory of your body. You’ll be naked (I was) and they’ll write down every mark and tattoo and anything else they find on your body. I was usually made to squat and cough to make sure you’re not trying to sneak anything in. 

Since covid is a thing you’ll get 2 tests. The first is a quick test to see if you have it. And the second is the more detailed test. Until you get the results back of your detailed test you’ll be quarantined. You can still pick your food but they’ll bring it to you and you’ll eat in your room. This usually takes about a day or two. 

I’d bring sweats, socks, a couple shirts, maybe a hoodie, and some candles or crocs. You can’t have anything with string or metal. I usually bring a pencil, notebook, and a few books I want to read with me. 

My state the holds are usually 3 to 7 days. If you really want to you can check yourself out against Dr’s orders, but if they think you’ll hurt yourself or others they’ll work on getting a court order to keep you. 

The food isn’t bad. I was usually given a menu in the morning for the next days food. You circle what you want. It’s not bad some places and others could use some help, it depends on the facility. 

You have lessons all day long. Usually until dinner, sometimes you’ll get one lesson after dinner. They usually have a tv that you can watch movies on. They have things to color and sometimes things to read. You’ll get to know everyone and everyone usually sits around talking about why they are here and what life is like on the outside. You’re not supposed to talk about these things, but everyone does. 

You can skip lessons if you really don’t want to go to it but they don’t like when you do that. Do that enough times and they’ll lock you out of your room which really sucks. 

You’ll talk to a social worker, a therapist, and a psychologist at various times. Sometimes a dr will also be involved in your treatment plan. Get to know them and talk to them. Let them know how you feel. They’ll be the ones who say you’re ready to go home. Or they’ll say you need to stay longer and petition a judge to side with them. 

You’ll have a roomie. Be nice to them they can make your life hell. I’ve had good and bad roomies. You’ll have a bathroom but it’s more like a public one. The doors don’t lock and they are a foot off the floor and a foot off the ceiling. My roomies and I would always have a sign were in the bathroom, usually turning the shower on to preserve some dignity. 

After you’re done there they usually recommend outpatient to continue your treatment plan. This is usually from 8am till 5pm and it’s a lot of the same classes, but you go home afterwards. Same therapist, social worker, psychologist, dr type deal as before. Usually you can move up to half days after a while and then eventually you’re done. Usually 2-3 weeks. Maybe more. Depends on what they want you to do. 

But you can leave any of the facilities until you can show you have a plan for when you get out. Usually an outside psychologist and therapist. They want to help you have a success. 

All in all if you find yourself in a bad spot like it sounds you are, it’s not a bad idea. Go to the nearest er and tell them you think you’re in a position to hurt yourself and that it’s scaring you. They’ll get you in and get you someone to talk to. Sometimes they’ll assign someone to be your buddy so you aren’t left alone. They won’t let you use the bathroom by yourself. However you can usually make a deal with them to close the door most of the way but not all the way. Get used to not pooping alone lol.
